title: Shadows Move
learning_objectives: Explain what a shadow is and why its length and direction change during the day
Compare an explanation text with a story on the same topic

factual_claims.claim: A shadow is the dark area behind an object that blocks light.
factual_claims.source: NASA Space Place, 'What is a shadow?' / Britannica Kids, 'Shadow'

factual_claims.claim: Shadows point away from the light source.
factual_claims.source: Britannica Kids, 'Shadow'; BBC Bitesize KS2 'Light and shadows'

factual_claims.claim: When the Sun is low in the sky (morning and evening) shadows are long; when it is high (midday) shadows are short.
factual_claims.source: BBC Bitesize KS2 'How do shadows change during the day?'; NOAA SciJinks

factual_claims.claim: The Sun appears to move across the sky because the Earth is turning.
factual_claims.source: NASA Space Place, 'What causes day and night?'

factual_claims.claim: People long ago used the Sun's shadow on a marked surface (a sundial) to tell the time.

parent_prompts: Before: Nia's shadow moved all day. Let's find out exactly why.
Try it: a torch and a pencil standing in clay. Move the torch low, high, low on the other side.
After: what would happen to Nia's stones on a cloudy day?

pages.text: Stand in the sun and you will see a dark shape on the ground, the same shape as you. That is your shadow.
pages.illustration_brief: A child standing on a path with a clear shadow beside; bright sun.
pages.audio_script: Stand in the sun and you will see a dark shape on the ground, the same shape as you. That is your shadow.
pages.image_alt: A child standing on a path with a clear shadow beside; bright sun.

pages.text: A shadow is made when something blocks light. Your body stops the sunlight from reaching the ground behind you, so that patch stays dark.
pages.illustration_brief: Diagram: sun rays hitting a figure; behind the figure a dark patch on the ground where rays are blocked.
pages.audio_script: A shadow is made when something blocks light. Your body stops the sunlight from reaching the ground behind you, so that patch stays dark.

vocabulary.definition: Gets in the way so something cannot pass.

pages.image_alt: Sun rays hitting a figure; behind the figure a dark patch where rays are blocked.

pages.text: Shadows always point away from the light. If the sun is on your left, your shadow is on your right.
pages.illustration_brief: Figure with sun on the left and shadow stretching to the right; an arrow from sun through the figure into the shadow.
pages.audio_script: Shadows always point away from the light. If the sun is on your left, your shadow is on your right.
pages.image_alt: Figure with sun on the left and shadow stretching to the right; an arrow through.

pages.text: When the sun is low, near the ground, light comes in sideways and your shadow stretches out long. That is why morning shadows are tall.
pages.illustration_brief: Low sun near the horizon; long stretched shadow.
pages.audio_script: When the sun is low, near the ground, light comes in sideways and your shadow stretches out long. That is why morning shadows are tall.
pages.image_alt: Low sun near the horizon; long stretched shadow.

pages.text: When the sun is high overhead, light comes almost straight down. Your shadow shrinks to a small shape at your feet. That is midday.
pages.illustration_brief: Sun directly overhead; tiny shadow under the figure.
pages.audio_script: When the sun is high overhead, light comes almost straight down. Your shadow shrinks to a small shape at your feet. That is midday.

vocabulary.definition: The middle of the day, around twelve o'clock, when the sun is highest.

pages.image_alt: Sun directly overhead; tiny shadow under the figure.

pages.text: The sun seems to cross the sky from one side to the other. Really, it is the Earth that is turning, like a slow spinning top, carrying you round to face the sun and then away.
pages.illustration_brief: Small Earth with a curved arrow showing rotation; the Sun fixed to one side; a tiny figure on the Earth.
pages.audio_script: The sun seems to cross the sky from one side to the other. Really, it is the Earth that is turning, like a slow spinning top, carrying you round to face the sun and then away.
pages.image_alt: Small Earth with a curved arrow showing rotation; the Sun fixed to one side; a tiny figure.

pages.text: Because the sun's place in the sky keeps changing, your shadow keeps changing too: long, short, long again, and swinging round from one side to the other.
pages.illustration_brief: Three-panel strip: morning long shadow left, midday short, evening long shadow right.
pages.audio_script: Because the sun's place in the sky keeps changing, your shadow keeps changing too: long, short, long again, and swinging round from one side to the other.
pages.image_alt: Three-panel strip: morning long shadow left, midday short, evening long shadow right.

pages.text: Long ago, people used this to tell the time. A stick in the ground and marks around it made a sun clock, called a sundial. Nia's stones were a sundial too.
pages.illustration_brief: A simple sundial: a stick casting a shadow onto marks arranged in an arc on the ground.
pages.audio_script: Long ago, people used this to tell the time. A stick in the ground and marks around it made a sun clock, called a sundial. Nia's stones were a sundial too.

vocabulary.definition: A clock that uses the shadow of a stick to show the time.
vocabulary.example: The garden has an old stone sundial.

pages.image_alt: A stick casting a shadow onto marks arranged in an arc on the ground.

quiz.prompt: Why are shadows short at midday?

options.text: The sun is high and light comes almost straight down
It is too hot for shadows

quiz.prompt: Why does the sun seem to cross the sky?

options.text: The sun flies around the Earth

quiz.prompt: In the story, Nia's shadow was tiny at lunchtime. Which page of this book explains why?

options.text: The page about the sun being high overhead
The page about standing in the sun

quiz.explanation: Page 5 explains that at midday the sun is high and the shadow shrinks to a small shape, which is what Nia saw at lunch.

quiz.prompt: Explain to a grown-up why a shadow is long in the morning and short at midday.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says shadows change; with support: mentions the sun moving, with prompting; independent: low sun gives sideways light and long shadow, high sun gives straight-down light and short shadow, because the Earth turns
quiz.explanation: Linking sun height to shadow length is the core idea of both books.

pairs.right: the sun had crossed the sky
